Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NexGen Renewables Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants are asked to limit themselves to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexGen Renewables Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Riley Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. NexGen Renewables delivered exceptional results in the Q3, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance, starting with our strategic priorities and outlook for the next quarter and year. Thank you, and good morning, everyone. As we wrap up another strong quarter with revenue of $1.45 billion, up 52% year-over-year, and adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 28.4%—driven by our record deployments—let me turn to our strategic priorities and outlook for the balance of 2024 and into 2025. We're laser-focused on three pillars: accelerating our project backlog execution, scaling next-generation clean tech innovations, and fortifying supply chain resilience amid a rapidly evolving global landscape. This positions NexGen to capture our fair share of the $1.7 trillion in global clean energy investments projected by BloombergNEF through 2030.

Priority one: backlog execution and commercial momentum for next quarter. In Q4 2024, we'll prioritize commissioning 1.8 GW of contracted projects, with 70% weighted toward high-IRR utility-scale solar-plus-storage hybrids in the U.S. Southwest and Texas ERCOT markets. This includes the 650 MW Phase II expansion of our Gemini Solar project in Nevada, co-developed with our partner Primergy Solar, which integrates 300 MWh of Tesla Megapack BESS for firming dispatchable power. Expect Q4 revenue of $1.55 billion to $1.65 billion, representing 15-20% sequential growth, with EPC margins holding steady at 22-24% thanks to optimized PPAs averaging $35/MWh—well below the U.S. PPA benchmark of $42/MWh per LevelTen Energy.

Regionally, U.S. operations remain our growth engine, bolstered by $500 million in IRA tax credits claimed YTD, including the full 45X domestic content adder for our U.S.-made bifacial TOPCon modules. In Europe, we'll advance 400 MW of onshore wind repowers in Germany and the UK, leveraging the EU's REPowerEU plan and falling turbine costs—down 12% YoY per IRENA data—to secure €150 million in new PPAs at €45/MWh. APAC exposure is ramping via our 200 MW floating solar initiative in Southeast Asia, tapping into ASEAN's 15 GW annual pipeline amid hydropower variability.

Priority two: innovation pipeline and technology leadership for full-year 2025 outlook. Looking to 2025, R&D capex will rise 25% to $250 million, targeting three breakthroughs: perovskite-silicon tandem cells hitting 32% module efficiency surpassing LONGi's 30.5% lab record, 8-hour iron-air flow batteries for long-duration storage to address duck curve challenges, and green hydrogen electrolyzers scaled to 100 MW via our JV with Plug Power. These aren't pie-in-the-sky; our pilot 50 MW tandem line in Arizona is already yielding 28% pilot efficiency, positioning us to undercut crystalline silicon LCOE by 15% at scale.

We'll allocate $2.5 billion in FY25 capex—60% to U.S. manufacturing expansions, including a 5 GW TOPCon fab in Ohio qualifying for full IRA Section 45X credits—and 25% to 2 GW of BESS deployments. This supports full-year 2025 guidance of $6.2-$6.8 billion in revenue, up 25-35% YoY, with EBITDA margins expanding to 34-36%. Our 12 GW backlog, 85% contracted through 2026 at blended $38/MWh, provides 3x visibility, while a 15 GW development pipeline—fueled by 500 MW of new awards in Q3—de-risks growth.

Priority three: supply chain resilience and market expansion. Geopolitical headwinds persist—Chinese module prices have cratered 25% to $0.22/Wp per InfoLink Consulting, squeezing ASPs—but our 40% U.S. vertical integration shields us, with domestic polysilicon costs 20% above spot but locked via long-term offtakes. We're diversifying with $300 million in India solar cell investments, eyeing 20% CAGR in that market per Wood Mackenzie, and exploring Latin America's 10 GW auction pipeline, starting with a 300 MW bid in Brazil's CEMIG auction.

Key headwinds include interest rate sensitivity—every 50 bps Fed hike trims IRR by 80 bps—and interconnection queues, now averaging 4.5 years per Lawrence Berkeley Lab. But tailwinds abound: U.S. data center demand could add 50 GW of load by 2030 per EPRI, with hyperscalers like Google committing 24/7 carbon-free power. In offshore wind, we're JV-ing on a 1 GW U.S. East Coast project akin to Ørsted's South Fork, targeting BOEM lease rounds.

In summary, NexGen is executing flawlessly in a market where clean energy now undercuts fossil fuels in 90% of global auctions per RMI. We're raising our 2025 EPS outlook to $4.25-$4.75 and initiating a 15 GW five-year pipeline target.

The other aspects—our development pipeline additions and milestones, revenue and earnings growth, CAPEX and OPEX details, impact of government incentives, operating capacity and generation output, and new PPAs secured—will be covered in detail by my colleagues.

Now, I'll hand over the call to Jordan Lee to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our financial performance in the Q3 was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.45 billion, representing a 52% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 42.1%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $142 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $218 million, or $0.72 per share. We ended the quarter with $850 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Let me dive deeper into some of these areas. Starting with revenue and earnings growth analysis. Good afternoon, everyone. Today, I'll dive deep into our revenue and earnings growth story, which continues to outperform both our internal targets and the broader industry benchmarks. The renewable energy sector is navigating a perfect storm of tailwinds—accelerating global decarbonization mandates, plummeting hardware costs, and supportive policies like the U.S. Inflation Reduction Act and the EU's REPowerEU plan—while grappling with supply chain headwinds and merchant price volatility.

Q3 revenue came in at $1.45 billion, a robust 52% year-over-year increase and 18% quarter-over-quarter growth, smashing our guidance. This marks our ninth straight quarter of accelerating revenue growth, driven by a 65% surge in contracted deployments and a 28% expansion in our backlog to $12.8 billion, with 70% now backlogged through FY2026. Full-year FY2024 revenue guidance is raised to $5.6–$5.9 billion, implying 48–55% YoY growth, well ahead of the S&P Global Clean Energy Index's consensus 25–30% sector growth.

Net income attributable to common shareholders was $218 million, or $0.72 diluted EPS, up 68% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA hit $412 million, a 61% YoY jump, with margins expanding 420 basis points to 28.4%. This profitability leap reflects not just top-line scale but disciplined cost management amid softening polysilicon prices, which fell another 15% QoQ to around $8/kg.

Segment breakdown: Solar PV systems, 52% of revenue at $754 million, up 67% YoY, fueled by 2.8 GWdc of new utility-scale deployments, primarily TOPCon modules with 23.5% average efficiency. Key wins included a 1.2 GWdc PPA with Southern California Edison under IRA tax credit transferability, and our first 500 MWdc bifacial project in Texas' ERCOT market. Energy storage solutions, 28% of revenue at $406 million, explosive 89% YoY growth, with 1.4 GWh shipped—led by our LFP-based BESS at 4-hour duration. Wind and hybrid projects, 12% at $174 million, steady 32% YoY from 850 MW of onshore turbine orders. Services and O&M, 8% at $116 million, 25% YoY uptick from our 8.5 GW fleet under management.

Geographically, North America drove 55% of growth at $798 million, up 72% YoY, supercharged by IRA credits. Europe $435 million, up 41% YoY. APAC $174 million, grew 35% YoY.

Gross margins expanded to 42.1% up 310 bps YoY, thanks to scale efficiencies, supply chain tailwinds, and product mix shift. OpEx as % of revenue fell to 14.2%. Free cash flow $285 million.

YoY, we're outpacing the sector. Strategically, doubling down on electrification adjacencies. Risks mitigated by reforms and localization. Our momentum underscores execution edge in $1.7T TAM. Raising FY2024 adjusted EBITDA to $1.65–$1.75 billion.

Next, capital expenditure and operating expense details. Our total CAPEX for Q3 came in at $385 million, bringing year-to-date spend to $1.05 billion—up 22% YoY, in line with $1.4 to $1.6 billion for FY24. This reflects aggressive buildout of 2.5 GW pipeline across solar PV, onshore wind, BESS, and green hydrogen.

CAPEX breakdown: 42% or $161 million to CIP, $95 million to SunForge Solar including 450 MW Nevada Phase II with TOPCon bifacial modules. 28% or $108 million to wind like 250 MW GaleForce Texas. 20% $77 million to BESS like 200 MWh IronPeak California. 10% $39 million to green H2 like 50 MW HyNova Rotterdam.

North America 55%, Europe 30%, APAC 15%. EPC inflation moderated to 3-4% YoY.

OPEX $142 million, up 2% YoY per MW, $34/kW intensity. O&M 48% $68 million, reduced curtailment via AI. SG&A 25% $36 million flat. R&D 13% $18 million on perovskites and flow batteries. G&A 14% $20 million.

Positioned for FCF, Q3 EBITDA margins 68%, ROIC 12-14%. FY25 CAPEX $1.8-2.0B. OPEX per MW decline 8-10%.

On the impact of government incentives and subsidies, these are foundational, underpinning 28% of Q3 revenue—up from 22% YoY—and $145 million to EBITDA, 35% increase.

U.S. IRA unlocked $1.2B YTD transferable credits. SunForge qualified for 30% ITC +10% domestic +10% energy communities, effective 50%. Wind PTC $25-32/MWh. Monetized 85% upfront.

Europe €220M or 18% revenue, REPowerEU, EEG, CfD at €65/MWh.

APAC China UHVDC, India PLI INR 4,500 crore, LatAm Proinfa R$1.2B.

Shift to performance-based favors our stack. Incentives lower IRR from 9.2% to 12.8%. Backlog 15 GW 60% attached. Diversifying via lobbying, hedging, innovation, manufacturing.

Building subsidy-optional model, 40% merchant-viable.

Operating capacity in MW and generation output in GWh: At Q3 end, 6,847 MW operating, 22% YoY increase from net 1,056 MW additions like 450 MW Gemini Solar + Storage, 320 MW Texas wind, 286 MW Spain solar.

Breakdown: Solar 3,212 MW 47%, wind onshore 2,456 MW 36%, offshore 685 MW 10%, BESS 494 MW 7%.

Regions: NA 4,021 MW 59%, EMEA 1,923 MW 28%, APAC 903 MW 13%.

Q4 adds 1,200-1,400 MW including 600 MW floating solar Australia, 800 MW Borssele.

Generation: 4,728 GWh Q3, 15% YoY up, capacity factor 24.8% improved 180 bps via AI SCADA.

Solar 22.1%, onshore wind 32.6%, offshore 41.2%. NA 2,891 GWh, EMEA 1,156, APAC 681.

FY24 17,200-17,600 GWh, 16% up. Hybrid focus, repowering unlock yield. Pipeline advancing.

New PPAs secured and average PPA price: Secured over 1.2 GW new PPAs, backlog to 4.8 GW up 35% YoY.

New wins: 450 MW PG&E CAISO 15-yr, 500 MW hyperscaler ERCOT 20-yr $28/MWh base, 250 MW PJM floating solar.

Average $32/MWh levelized, 12% premium to prior, up 18% YoY. Tailwinds: post-cliff stabilization, higher WACC, tech edge.

CAISO $38/MWh, ERCOT merchant upside, PJM capacity. De-risks 65% pipeline, 12-14% IRRs. Offtake 55% utilities 35% corporates. Q3 bids 2 GW, FY new 2.5-3 GW $31-34/MWh.

I'll now turn the call over to Taylor Kim to discuss our project development activities.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 28.2 GW gross of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies—our net at 14.1 GW. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

In detail on development pipeline additions and project milestones: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Our development pipeline additions and key project milestones underscore our leadership in delivering shovel-ready projects, leveraging IRA Section 45X/ITC adders and corporate PPA demand from hyperscalers targeting RE100.

Q3 added 4.8 GW gross, total 28.2 GW across 150+ projects, up 15% QoQ 42% YoY. Net 14.1 GW top quartile.

By tech: Solar 3.0 GW 62%, wind 950 MW 20%, BESS 575 MWh 12%, emerging 275 MW 6%.

Regions: U.S. 2.6 GW 55%, Europe 1.1 GW 25%, APAC/LatAm 1.1 GW 20%.

Milestones: 12 major, 2.3 GW advanced. PPAs 1.8 GW incl. 850 MW Rattlesnake with Meta $45/MWh. Permits 1.1 GW, FID 450 MW Ohio wind, NTP 750 MW Desert Bloom/Prairie Rose. Grid sync Horizon BESS 95% efficiency.

"Queue-First" playbook, $150M deposits. Hybrids 35%. U.S.-sourced 85%. Q4 adds 3-4 GW, 2 GW NTP, $5B tax equity.

This gives 5+ years visibility.

Dr. Elena Vasquez, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Taylor. We are dedicated to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing advanced technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. We believe that these technologies will play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

Next, Marcus Hale will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Sustainability is a core value at NexGen Renewables, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability.

Now, Riley Patel will provide operational highlights.

Riley Patel:
Thank you, Marcus. Our operational performance remains strong. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.

I'll turn it back to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Riley. To summarize, NexGen Renewables had an exceptional Q3. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our focus on sustainability will drive continued growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks for the question, John. Our international expansion is a key part of our strategy, as outlined earlier. In Europe, we're advancing 400 MW of onshore wind repowers in Germany and the UK under REPowerEU, with €150 million in PPAs. In APAC, our 200 MW floating solar in Southeast Asia taps ASEAN's pipeline, and we're investing $300 million in India for 20% CAGR. Latin America sees us bidding 300 MW in Brazil and pursuing Chile's Atacama projects. This diversification fortifies resilience, with 20-25% of our pipeline outside the U.S., targeting policy tailwinds like EU Taxonomy and India's PLI.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Lisa. Intermittency is core to our innovation focus. We're scaling hybrids—now 35% of pipeline—with BESS like Tesla Megapacks and our iron-air flow batteries for 8-hour LDS, addressing duck curves. Our Gemini and Rattlesnake projects integrate solar-plus-storage for dispatchable power, achieving 70-80% firming. Pilots like Horizon BESS show 95% round-trip efficiency for frequency services, and green H2 electrolyzers add flexibility. These stack IRRs 300 bps above standalone, meeting hyperscaler 24/7 CF demands.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Rodriguez:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Jordan Lee:
Absolutely, Mike. Incentives are accelerants, driving 28% of Q3 revenue and $145M EBITDA. IRA's ITC/PTC stack to 50% effective on $800M capex, monetized upfront via JPMorgan tax equity. Europe CfD/EEG €220M, APAC/ LatAm PLI/Proinfa. They boost IRR 350 bps to 12.8%, but our LCOE $25-30/MWh makes 40% merchant-viable. We're lobbying extensions, hedging changes, and ramping U.S. manufacturing for bonuses.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Patel:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Alex Rivera:
Emily, demand growth is a massive tailwind. U.S. data centers alone add 50 GW by 2030 per EPRI, with Google/Microsoft committing 24/7 CF power—hence our hyperscaler PPAs like Meta's 850 MW. Global electrification, AI loads, and coal phase-outs fuel 15%+ annual adds per BloombergNEF. Our 28.2 GW pipeline and hybrids position us to capture share, with FY25 revenue up 25-35% and 15 GW 5-year target.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for any closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of NexGen Renewables. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
